back: Growth from within: more sales, new products or new markets.
Growth by joining with another business through a merger or a takeover.
Merger: two businesses agree to join. Takeover: one buys control of another, possibly against its managers' wishes.
Joining with a business at the same stage of the same industry (e.g. two bakeries).
Joining with a supplier (backward) or a customer (forward) in the same chain of production.
Joining with a business in an unrelated industry, to spread risk.
Profit, economies of scale, market share, security, status.
Poor communication, cash shortages, loss of control, low motivation, diseconomies of scale.
Internal: slow, lower risk, keeps control. External: fast, costly, culture clashes, removes competitors.
